tagline: A belle-époque seaside city on the Basque coast, San Sebastián curves around La Concha bay and has one of the world's great food scenes, from pintxos bars to Michelin stars.
overview: San Sebastián, or Donostia in Basque, sits on the Bay of Biscay near the French border. It became a fashionable resort in the 19th century when the Spanish royal family summered here, leaving elegant promenades, a seafront casino and the Miramar Palace.

La Concha, a shell-shaped bay with a sandy city beach, is framed by Monte Urgull and Monte Igueldo, whose old funicular climbs to a famous viewpoint. Ondarreta beach and Zurriola, a surfing beach, complete the waterfront.

The city is famous for food: it has one of the highest numbers of Michelin stars per person in the world, and the Parte Vieja's bars are piled with pintxos. The San Sebastián International Film Festival takes place every September, and the Jazzaldia festival in July.
